content:
Public failure mode (Claude Code 4.7 + dot-file hierarchy rot): User on r/Anthropic (Neat-Nectarine814, 9-month CC Max user, has used Cursor, Copilot, GPT-4 across that period) reported 4.7 regression with specific symptoms — model stalls on questions already answered, hallucinates file contents, refuses to iterate after declaring done, asks brain-dead clarification questions instead of doing work. The stalling burns tokens, pushes user across compaction threshold, compaction lands mid-conversation and erases the working state. Self-reinforcing cascade: stalling causes compaction causes context loss causes more stalling on rebuilt thread.

Diagnostic hypothesis (developed across two Reddit thread responses, second one corrected by Anthony): The proximate cause looks like a single CLAUDE.md being stale, but the deeper cause is the dot-file hierarchy itself. Claude Code reads a stack — ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md global, then walks up the directory tree picking up every CLAUDE.md it finds. Plus AGENTS.md, .claude/ directories, .cursorrules from old Cursor sessions, .windsurfrules, copilot config fragments. Multi-platform users over multi-month spans accumulate contradictory dot-files describing codebase states that no longer exist. Model tries to reconcile contradictory priors before reading actual files, defaults to asking clarification questions (looks like stalling, actually is non-hallucination behavior), eventually gives up and trusts the dot-files over the conversation. The fresh-chat circuit breaker does not help because every fresh chat re-loads the same contradictory hierarchy.

Why this maps onto the broader pattern Anthony has been documenting: same shape as test-session-hook-777 bug (write-path/read-path divergence reading state from different sources), same shape as close_session/spiral_inherit mental-model failure (architecture working correctly but operator assumptions about primitives are wrong). The dot-file rot is infrastructure rot. The model is not regressing in the way users describe; the operator-side context substrate has accumulated drift that 4.7 is more sensitive to than 4.6 was, possibly because 4.7 leans harder on provided project context (a reasonable design decision that surfaces previously-hidden infrastructure rot as a perceived model regression).

Predictions if hypothesis holds: (1) Users with clean, recently-maintained single-source CLAUDE.md report 4.7 working fine. (2) Users with multi-month accumulated dot-files across multiple agent platforms report 4.7 broke their workflow. (3) Running `find ~ -name CLAUDE.md -o -name .cursorrules -o -name AGENTS.md 2>/dev/null` will return surprising counts for affected users. (4) Cleaning the dot-file stack to one canonical file per active project, deleting orphan globals, removing agents-not-currently-used residue, will measurably reduce stalling and compaction frequency.

What this is NOT: a Sovereign Stack pitch. The mitigation is dot-file hygiene, available to any CC user without infrastructure investment. Pitching the stack into this pain would be the failure mode the thread was already recovering from.

Logging as public failure mode for chronicle reference. If the diagnostic question lands with Neat-Nectarine814 and they report back, update with empirical confirmation or refutation. If others report similar symptoms, the dot-file-rot hypothesis is testable and the fix is mechanical.
